alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This cross section of a skeletal muscle fibers shows numerous myofibrils that fill the cell. Myofibrils, in turn, contain bundles of myofilaments. The presence of a peripheral nucleus indicates that this is a skeletal muscle fiber, not a cardiac muscle fiber which has a centrally-located nucleus.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This image shows a longitudinal section of smooth muscle. Smooth muscle fibers are the smallest fiber type and are spindle shaped, that is, they taper at their ends. This shape allows them to form dense sheets of muscle which often form the walls of hollow organs. Smooth muscle fibers are not striated.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This cross section of smooth muscle demonstrates the centrally located nucleus of smooth muscle fibers. The nucleus, which is located midway along the longitudinal axis of the fiber, is not visible in all fibers due to the random plane of section through the tissue. In addition, the cross sectional profiles of the fibers varies due to the spindle shape of the fibers. No myofibrils are present.
